A new research project will begin in February on the topic of "Electromobility Data for Interdisciplinary Studies" (EDIS). Some information in the slides attached (text in French) In the context of this project, Mines Saint-Étienne has funding for a PhD that will be co-advised by Maxime Lefrançois, Antoine Zimmermann, and Amel Fraisse (U. Lille).

The topic will most probably revolve around the following main research hypothesis:

"Semantic Web and NLP technologies can be combined to facilitate the exploration, linkage with territorial and contextual data, and visualization, of multidisciplinary research results"

Some precisions:

* The research results this PhD will focus on are the ones of former research projects and other work packages in the EDIS project, including e-vehicle technical datasets (ex. data from hundreds of sensor equipping electric vehicles), and qualitative interviews results (social science)
* This PhD, the EDIS project, and the set of related research projects EDIS is part of (PEPR MOBIDEC), all aim at the Digitalization and Decarbonization of Mobility in general.
* This PhD is related to the notion of Open Data / Data Space (we'll contribute to the MobSciDat data platform, an instance of OpenDataSoft),
* Data visualizations in this context aim to communicate results to various audiences (experts, citizens, journalists),

We first offer a research internship starting Feb./April. 2026, as one way test a candidate and bootstrap the PhD.

The internship topic is "Characterization and semantization of qualitative and technical e-mobility test datasets and linkage with territorial and contextual data". It aims to get the future PhD candidate familiar with the type of data we're manipulating, and understand the type of linkage that could be interesting to get more insight from this data. This first case study involves data collected from a Nissan Leaf, including time-series vehicle data (about 100 CSV files with 118 variables), GPS traces, and external contextual information (e.g., weather, elevation, traffic, and air quality).

We expect candidates to have good knowledge and skills related to Data Interoperability, Semantic Web technologies, and/or NLP, and an interest in interdisciplinary research mixing Science and Technical studies and Social Sciences with social and territorial aspects. Experience of data visualization is a plus.

If you are interested, please feel free to send me your application directly by email.
